summary: The plan has multiple blockers and high-severity gaps against both the stated ask and the repository’s current contracts.

findings.summary: Schema upgrades are explicitly routed to the old partial-repair path, not full re-derivation.
findings.detail: A.1 says schema version 2 should force every profile through re-derivation, but A.2 classifies a contract mismatch as “stop — existing L488-493 behavior, unchanged.” The current behavior at skills/clodex/SKILL.md:488-492 asks for only the missing/stale keys and rewrites only those keys. Thus requirement 2—the newer-version case—does not reliably converge on full re-derivation.

findings.summary: The proposed `--bare` Claude commands cannot load the clodex skills they invoke.
findings.detail: B.3 invokes `claude -p --bare "/clodex …"`, while the plan’s own evidence says `--bare` skips skills, commands, subagents, plugins, MCP, memory, CLAUDE.md, and OAuth/keychain credentials. B.10 merely says to pass context explicitly; it never specifies how all five clodex skills, templates, settings, and routing handoffs are supplied. It also selects `dontAsk` without defining the required per-stage allowlist, so write operations and state appends would be denied. The topology cannot execute as written.

findings.summary: A mandate declaration in a lane brief does not create the standing mandate needed for unattended approval.
findings.detail: Current clodex requires an actual `approval:granted` event with `scope: "mandate"`, bound to the current plan hash and originally granted by the user (skills/clodex-plan/SKILL.md:420-447; docs/clodex-design.md:205-215). B.5 adds only prose to the brief, while gate 7 prohibits any `by: "user"` event during unattended runs. Nothing turns the declaration into a valid standing event. Direction approval, finding dispositions, and final plan approval therefore still prompt or stall, so requirement 6 is not met.

findings.summary: Skipping `clodex-ship` makes the claimed handoff artifact and `handed-off` terminal state impossible.
findings.detail: B.3 says ship is not run, yet B.8 says a clean lane parks at ship with a handoff and treats `handed-off` as its terminal state. Current clodex creates and records that artifact only in ship after final review and release authorization, then appends `release:updated`, `run:closed`, and archives the run (skills/clodex-ship/SKILL.md:1831-1872, 2033-2061, 2250-2261). Release authorization is explicitly non-delegable. The proposed lane can neither reach the claimed state nor preserve its evidence after worktree removal.

findings.summary: The universal tracked-profile probe has no valid first-run ordering.
findings.detail: A.2 runs `git ls-files --error-unmatch .clodex/profile.json` as part of universal check 7. In a never-bootstrapped repository that necessarily fails. A.6 deletes the existing special ordering at skills/clodex/SKILL.md:178-181 but never states a replacement ordering that runs inspection/interview before this probe. Requirement 1 is therefore not checkably satisfied.

findings.summary: The orchestrator bypasses the only current profile validator and bootstrap-currency entry point.
findings.detail: The only current whole-profile validation is the router call at skills/clodex/SKILL.md:462-475. Stage skills load the profile directly; ship’s schema reads at skills/clodex-ship/SKILL.md:604, 802, and 1273 inspect only the action field set and do not read profile `schema_version`. B.3 invokes `/clodex-build` and `/clodex-verify` directly after the initial plan session, bypassing the proposed router preflight and bootstrap check. A schema or skill update during a run can therefore enter later stages unchecked, and the plan does not account for this consumer topology.

findings.summary: Skill-version currency depends on an unowned, unenforced manual `VERSION` bump.
findings.detail: A.1 says a release process will bump `skills/clodex/VERSION`, but no such file or release process exists in the repo, and no proposed test or gate owns the bump. Installation is by symlink plus `git pull` (README.md:26-27), so a changed SKILL.md with an unchanged VERSION is entirely legal. That defeats the newer-version convergence guarantee for every future non-schema skill change.

findings.summary: The bootstrap schema and fingerprint are too incomplete and internally circular to implement reliably.
findings.detail: The plan gives an example object, not its full JSON Schema: required child fields, types, formats, marker vocabulary, and canonical hash serialization are unspecified. The fixed marker manifest is described only as “~25 paths,” despite claims that it discovers arbitrary second workspace package files. The fingerprint also includes `profile.commands.*`, but first-run inspection occurs before a profile exists and re-derivation may change those commands after the fingerprint is computed. Changes to a package script’s command body with the same key are not detected because only key names are included. A reader cannot determine a correct implementation or test oracle.

findings.summary: Worktree behavior is contradictory and has no migration protocol for existing lanes.
findings.detail: A.2 says repo drift in a linked worktree is merely recorded and that only contract drift stops a lane. A.3 says any worktree needing re-derivation “says so and stops.” Neither section explains how an already-forked lane obtains the new profile commit from the main checkout, how legitimate lane-local marker changes are distinguished, or when it can resume. This fails the requested existing-worktree production analysis.

findings.summary: Half-applied schema migration can strand or oscillate profiles between old and new installs.
findings.detail: There is no atomic profile rewrite, migration journal, minimum-reader version, or recovery rule. If schema v2 lands before the scripts/router text, all profiles fail with no derivation path. If a v2 profile is opened by an older v1 install, the old validator rejects schema_version 2 and current instructions direct it to rewrite only that value back to 1; the custom validator ignores additionalProperties, so the v2 bootstrap block can remain while versions oscillate. Active worktrees retain old profile commits and stop without a defined update path.

findings.summary: The topology is not Codex-heavy at most model-bearing stages.
findings.detail: B.4 lists 11 model-bearing stages: four Codex stages and seven Claude stages—five Opus and two Sonnet—before counting the separate deliverable-lane writer. Repo stages are also driven by Claude sessions. This does not satisfy requirement 4’s request to use Codex for heavy reasoning/execution at most stages.

findings.summary: Opus is retained at stages for which the cited research does not establish Opus superiority.
findings.detail: The table contains five Opus stages, contradicting its own “Four Opus stages” statement. The evidence supports Claude’s relative advantage for computer/MCP use and offers a small third-party code-review comparison, but the brief-authoring anecdote proves only that briefs matter, held-out-test research does not compare models as judges, and no cited comparison supports Opus for morning synthesis. Requirement 5 is therefore only gestured at for three of the five stages.

findings.summary: The plan never gives exact valid programmatic invocations for clodex’s review passes.
findings.detail: Topology labels commands as `codex exec --role …`, but `--role` belongs to `run-codex.sh`; its actual interface requires `--repo`, `--prompt-file`, inputs, and usually `--run-id` (skills/clodex/runner/run-codex.sh:11-16). Current exact review calls live at skills/clodex-plan/SKILL.md:543-549 and skills/clodex-build/SKILL.md:663-669, but the new orchestrator call contract is not specified. Deliverable lanes also call Codex directly despite the plan saying the runner remains the only path. Finally, not running ship skips clodex’s release-diff review at skills/clodex-ship/SKILL.md:358-360. Requirement 6 is unmet.

findings.summary: The 28 blocking gates are categorized but never mapped to concrete unattended behavior.
findings.detail: B.8 says “most” gates are pre-answered and gives three general responses, but it does not map each gate from the census to a brief field, mandate grant, or park transition. Several gates—dirty overlap, strays, red verification outcomes, review-cap funding, and exact-action approval—need distinct detection and state handling. Without that mapping, a worker can still emit an ordinary clodex question and exit successfully; no mechanism converts it into the required PARKED artifact without surfacing it.

findings.summary: The supposed held-out acceptance criterion is readable by the worker.
findings.detail: `run-plan.json` is committed before lanes fork and contains the acceptance-file path, while the acceptance file itself is under `docs/acceptance/` in the same repository. The lane brief explicitly tells the worker to read the committed orchestration plan. Nothing denies access to the acceptance file, so gate 13 is not “the check the worker never saw.” The cited SpecBench effect concerns genuinely hidden executable tests, not a repository-readable prose rubric evaluated by another Opus session.

findings.summary: The orchestrator has no crash-safe or overlap-safe state machine despite existing isomorphic prior art.
findings.detail: `orchestrator.ndjson` has no schema, reducer, atomic write discipline, run identity, lock, pending/done receipts, or replay rules. A crash after dispatch or another external action but before ledger append will duplicate work on restart; two instances can append the same ledger, dispatch the same lanes, and overwrite the same dated morning report. The repo already solves this class in skills/clodex/state/clodex_state.py:16-39 and docs/clodex-design.md:94-109, 148-152 with locks, append/fsync, deterministic rebuild, operation IDs, and reconcile-before-retry. The plan misses that isomorphic mechanism.

findings.summary: Parking has no unpark or recovery transition.
findings.detail: B.8 defines a PARKED markdown record and scheduling around the lane, but not how an answer is recorded, how dependencies are re-evaluated, which session or Codex invocation resumes, how stale permissions/flags are restored, or how a park at ship differs from a terminal handoff. A parked lane can therefore remain parked forever, exactly the production case the review asks to cover.

findings.summary: Owned paths are neither complete nor sufficiently specified, and the plan exceeds the stated two-script shape.
findings.detail: The plan names four new scripts (`inspect_repo.py`, `bootstrap_check.py`, `quota.py`, `orchestrate.py`), plus VERSION, run-plan data, acceptance files, a launchd definition, lane-brief template changes, reducer changes, and tests. Paths are not given for `orchestrate.py`, `quota.py`, run-plan schema/config, or launchd state. B.0 also leaves the skill rename undecided. Because no change owns this complete set, disjointness and completion cannot be checked.

findings.summary: The plan’s own tier accounting is arithmetically wrong.
findings.detail: B.6 says 11 of 14 gates are arithmetic, but gates 1-10 are the only arithmetic rows: 10 of 14. Gates 11-12 are artifacts, 13 is claimed tier 4, and 14 is prose. The following paragraph says three gates remain prose but names two concepts that are not numbered gates. The control-framework accounting is not internally checkable.

findings.summary: `counts.py` is not isomorphic to report-wide count reconciliation.
findings.detail: `counts.py` derives findings, dispositions, severities, open IDs, and invocation counts only (skills/clodex/state/counts.py:22-69). Lane reports also contain commit counts, evidence/debt counts, gate baselines, test counts, and conflict counts (skills/clodex/templates/lane-report.md:19-62). Gate 10’s promise that every integer in the report is regenerated from `counts.py` cannot be implemented with that script.

findings.summary: The proposed behavioral changes have no owned exploit/control tests.
findings.detail: The committed harness requires every engine, runner, or executable skill-fragment behavior change to add an exploit/control pair (tests/run.sh:8-10). The plan does not own tests for first-run bootstrap, version/fingerprint drift, worktree behavior, schema migration interruption, client-artifact completeness, effort retry, or overlapping orchestrators. B.9 says “with a test” but names no test file or assertions.

findings.summary: The plan changes documented behavior without owning documentation updates.
findings.detail: It does not update README.md:73 or skills/opus-orchestration/README.md:5-32 despite replacing/renaming that topology. Bootstrap/version/profile behavior changes require updates to skills/clodex/README.md:13-22, 130-149 and docs/clodex-design.md:58-70, 161-171. Making `client-artifact` mechanically usable requires updating docs/clodex-design.md:25-28, skills/clodex-plan/README.md:37-41, and skills/clodex-verify/README.md:32-36. The mandate and handed-off claims also conflict with docs/clodex-design.md:198-215 and the archive contract at lines 83-90.

findings.summary: The effort-retry recommendation transfers an Opus result to Codex without supporting evidence.
findings.detail: The measured cheap-effort/retry effect is for Opus 5 on SWE-bench Pro. The plan turns it into “the single cheapest change” for a Codex Terra implementer and retries every non-complete envelope, although `partial`, `interrupted`, `failed`, and usage errors are infrastructure/outcome states unlike benchmark task failures. No Codex effort-tier probe or pass/cost measurement supports medium→high, and current runner semantics normally resume partial work rather than start a benchmark-style retry.

findings.summary: The model-readback gate does not verify which Codex model actually ran.
findings.detail: Gate 3 uses Claude’s `modelUsage`, but local-harness-probes.md:134-138 says Codex’s event stream does not echo the actual model and verification must correlate against the richer rollout. The runner envelope records the requested model passed to its validator, not an independently observed model. The plan specifies neither rollout/session correlation nor race handling across four concurrent Codex calls, so it cannot catch silent Codex routing changes as claimed.

findings.summary: The claimed pressure to book `client-artifact` as debt is contradicted by the completeness code.
findings.detail: The tuple check at skills/clodex-verify/SKILL.md:711-713 runs over both evidence and debt items. Booking `client-artifact` as debt is rejected just like producing it as evidence; only dropping or relabeling the class can pass. The plan’s stated two pressured outcomes are therefore wrong.

findings.summary: The proposed deletion range would remove claims-ledger bootstrap behavior that has no replacement.
findings.detail: A.6 describes skills/clodex/SKILL.md:593-609 as only a repeated two-lanes incident. In fact lines 607-609 require multi-lane repositories to bootstrap `.clodex/claims.json` and reserve writes to the orchestrator. The incident itself is principally lines 601-606. Deleting the cited whole range drops existing concurrency behavior not restored elsewhere in A.

findings.summary: Load-bearing census and self-review evidence are not reproducible from the committed evidence.
findings.detail: The gate census labels itself unaudited model judgment, while the six structured reader returns and generator script it says produced the 119/47/28 counts are absent. The plan nevertheless treats 28 as exact. It also repeatedly cites a nonexistent §C for two self-review rounds, and no review envelopes are present. Local probes record quota movement from 7% to 9%, not the plan’s claimed 8% to 12%. These claims cannot be checked by another reader.

findings.summary: The `runtimes` warning citation starts one line earlier than stated.
findings.detail: The quoted warning begins at skills/clodex/SKILL.md:505, not line 506. The correct range is 505-508.

findings.summary: The inspection block contains seven shell commands, not nine.
findings.detail: The command block is skills/clodex/SKILL.md:497-504. Counting the semicolon-separated `ls` and `sed` separately yields seven commands: two on line 498, then two `ls` calls, `cat`, `git tag`, and `git symbolic-ref`.

findings.summary: The `client-artifact` grep rule is prose, not an arithmetic gate.
findings.detail: A.7 labels end-to-end vocabulary support arithmetic partly because of a Common-mistakes instruction to grep before committing. No script or test enforces that grep. The schema enum and verify tuple are arithmetic checks, but the proposed cross-file completeness rule remains tier 1.
